SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days.
  - Onset: 3 days ago
  - Frequency: 4–5 times daily
  - Nature: Mixture of watery and loose stools; no blood, no mucus
  - Associated symptoms: Mild abdominal pain, single episode of vomiting, mild (self-reported) fever, reduced appetite
  - No recent travel or dietary changes
  - Still drinking fluids adequately
- Past medical history: Asthma (status: active/unsure)
- Family history: Father deceased (age 62) due to bowel cancer; father also had hypertension
- Medications: "Laxepro" (inhaler; color yellow) – dose/route/frequency not documented
- Social history: Not documented
- Allergies: None reported

Objective:
- General: No clinical signs of dehydration (per clinician impression via video consultation)
- Vitals: Not documented
- Physical examination: Not documented beyond general appearance
- Investigations: None performed

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute Diarrhea
   - Assessment: Acute self-limiting diarrhea, likely viral or infective etiology
   - Differential diagnosis: None documented
   - Investigations planned: Stool sample only if diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool
   - Treatment planned:
     - Maintain oral hydration; consider Dioralyte (oral rehydration solution) over the counter
     - Dietary advice: Strict soft diet (e.g., crackers, toast, mashed vegetables); avoid dairy (except yogurt), meat, fish, and eggs until diarrhea resolves for at least 48 hours
     - Yogurt recommended for probiotic effect
     - Escalation plan: Seek further care if going to the toilet >6–8 times/day, if unable to tolerate fluids, or if signs of dehydration occur; contact clinic if diarrhea persists beyond a week or if blood/mucus in stool
   - Relevant referrals: None

2. Asthma
   - Assessment: History of asthma; using "Laxepro" inhaler (unclear if current/mainstay therapy)
   - Differential diagnosis: None documented
   - Investigations planned: None
   - Treatment planned: Continue current inhaler ("Laxepro" – dose/route/frequency not documented)
   - Relevant referrals: None

Quality checks:

●	Missing clinically expected elements: 
   - Detailed medication list and reconciliation
   - Asthma severity/control not assessed; inhaler type "Laxepro" unclear (potential transcription error or misunderstanding)
   - Vitals and physical examination findings not documented
   - Social history (e.g., smoking, alcohol) not discussed
●	Internal conflicts: None identified
●	Transcript quality: Occasional minor audio confusion (e.g., inhaler name), otherwise information generally clear.
